senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. יָגָה) [to feel pain,] to take pains, to labor; to be tired.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 58a:4">Ber. 58ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="J00086"><he>יְגִיעָה</he></cite>. Y. ib. V, 5ᶜ <he>אנו יָגַעְנוּ וכ׳</he> we have been busy at work for an entire day.

<cite ref="Berakhot 58a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>י׳ זה לשתי וכ׳</he> this one has worked (accomplished) more in two hours &c.; <cite ref="Berakhot 58a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>כך י׳ … בתורה וכ׳</he> so has R. Bun accomplished in studies in the twenty eight years (of his life) &c.; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:2:6">Cant. R. to VI, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:11:5">Koh. R. to V, 11</cite>.

<cite ref="Megillah 6b:3">Meg. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>אם יאמר … יָגַעְתִּי וכ׳</he> if one tells thee, ‘I have toiled (studied) and achieved nothing’, do not believe; ‘I have not toiled and have achieved’, do not believe &c.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:5:19">Y. Ber. IX, end, 14ᵈ</cite> <he>צריך לִיגַע בתורה</he> must study the Law.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 12:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. XII</cite>, beg. <he>חדלו מליגע בתורה</he> they ceased from studying the Law; a. fr.

Sot. II, 1 (14ᵃ) כדי לְיַגְּעָהּ (Rashi: לְיַי׳) in order to wear her out (so that she may be induced to confess). Sifra Vayikra, Ḥobah, Par. 5, ch. VII אבל אם היה מְיַגְּעָן וכ׳ but if after having troubled them (the judges) an entire day, he says finally &c.; Yalk. Lev. 469 היה מונע (corr. acc.); Tosef. Toh. VI, 14 ומשהגיע (read ומשהִגִּיעָן Hif.). Y. Bets. II, 61ᶜ bot. מתוך שאתה מְיַיגְּעוֹ וכ׳ because you put him to special trouble (by ordering a special form of cakes) &c.—

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 41:1">Ex. R. s. 41</cite> <he>התלמיד … יִגַּעְתִּיךָ</he> the pupil says to the teacher, I have wearied thee; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 161">Yalk. Sam. 161</cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>מְיוּגָּע</he>, pl. <he>מְיוּגָּעִים</he>, <he>מְיוּגָּעִין</he>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 8b">Keth. 8ᵇ</cite> <he>ואתם אחינו המ׳ המדוכאין וכ׳</he> and you, our brethren, who are worn out and crushed by this bereavement.
<cite ref="Tosefta Tahorot 6:14">Tosef. Toh. VI, 14</cite>, v. supra.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 39">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXXIX</cite>, beg. (ref. to <cite ref="Malachi 2:17">Mal. II, 17</cite>) <he>הוֹגַעְתֶּם לי במעשיכם וכ׳</he> (ed. Bub., differ.) it does not say, you wore me out with your doings, but with your words.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:28">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 36</cite> <he>והרב … רב לך כי הוֹגַעְתִּיךָ</he> and the teacher will say to the pupil, thou hast enough now, for I have wearied thee?; a. e.

<cite ref="Gittin 70a:22">Gitt. 70ᵃ</cite> <he>הבא בדרך ונ׳</he> who has been travelling and is tired. Pesik. Shub., p. 164ᵃ <he>שלא תִתְיַיגֵּעַ בחזירה</he> that you may not get tired on your way back.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 14:1">Pesik. R. s. 14</cite> <he>אני נִתְיַיגַּעְתִּי בה וכ׳</he> I took pains with her and smote her &c.; a. fr.
